sections.html:
Enterprise lies in the Wiregrass part of southeast Alabama. Most of it is in Coffee County, a western slice reaches into Dale County, and Fort Rucker, home of Army Aviation, is next door. The 2020 census put the population at 28,711, spread over 11,350 households.

Counting 12,531 housing units, the census found 9.4% empty. Homeowner vacancy was 2.9% and rental vacancy was 9.3%, which tells you vacant rentals are a bigger part of the picture than vacant owner-occupied houses. Median age is 35.9 years. Mail goes out under ZIP codes 36330 and 36331, and phones use area code 334.

On March 1, 2007, an EF4 tornado cut through town. Losses were estimated at nearly $307 million, and at least 647 houses were damaged or destroyed along a quarter-mile-wide path through downtown. Enterprise High School was rebuilt at the west end of Boll Weevil Circle and reopened August 23, 2010, with reinforced safe rooms.

Hurricanes reach this far inland as well. Eloise in 1975 and Opal in 1995 both did extensive damage here. Local buyers remember all of it, so storm questions come up early: how old is the roof, was anything rebuilt, who paid for it.

Keep permits and contractor receipts for any storm repair in one folder. An underwriter or title examiner may ask for them, and having them ready saves a round of phone calls.

  • Roofs: age, missing shingles and tarps left from earlier storms.
  • Trees: large limbs hanging over the roof or power lines.
  • Windows and doors: seals, storm shutters and past water intrusion.
  • Insurance: open claims or wind and hail deductibles that could shape an offer.

The 2020 figures show 25.5 percent of residents under 18 and 15.6 percent aged 65 or older. About 33.9 percent of households had children at home, and roughly 28 percent were one person living alone. Families upgrading, retirees downsizing and heirs settling an estate each show up in that mix.

Orders from the Army, a new employer or a family move can shrink the window for a sale to a few weeks. When you describe the house to a buyer, give the year it was built and say whether any section was rebuilt after a storm. One plain sentence like that heads off a lot of back and forth.

  • Owners with a transfer or relocation on a short clock.
  • Landlords whose tenants left behind damage.
  • Heirs who inherited a house and live in another state.
  • Owners of houses with older roofs, plumbing or heating and air systems.

The transfer becomes official when the new deed is filed with the probate office for the county holding the parcel. For most Enterprise addresses that means Coffee County, and for a smaller number it means Dale County. Your tax bill shows which one applies to you.

State law adds a recordation tax of 50 cents for every $500 of value, together with a form that states the true sale price. The rule sits in section 40-22-1 of the Alabama code. At closing the settlement agent collects the tax and sends the paperwork to the probate office, so you rarely deal with the clerk yourself.

Tax bills come due October 1 and go delinquent after December 31. A year's bill covers a full twelve months, so whoever handles your closing will divide it between you and the buyer by the days each of you held the house.

Ask early how the current year stands. Any open balance comes out of your sale proceeds at the table, because the lien rides with the property and not with the person who owed it.

sections.h2: Steps to sell an Enterprise house
sections.html:
Financed buyer or cash buyer, the paper trail follows roughly the same order.

StepWhat you doWho handles it
Gather papersLocate the deed and check that every owner's name matchesYou
PayoffRequest a payoff letter if a mortgage is still openYour lender
Condition listWrite down known repair problems so the buyer sees them up frontYou
Title searchLook for liens and gaps in the chain of ownershipTitle company or attorney
ClosingSign the deed, settle the tax split and file the deedClosing agent

Bring a photo ID to the closing, along with keys, garage openers and any warranty papers for the roof or the heating and air system. If more than one person is on the deed, every owner needs to sign.

sections.h2: What if the house needs work?
sections.html:
Older roofs, storm wear and deferred maintenance make a house hard to move on the open market, since a lender wants it to appraise and pass inspection. A cash purchase is not tied to a lender, so it can close on the date you choose and the buyer takes the house as it stands.

Cash does not erase the basics. A title search and the tax settlement still happen. What disappears is the appraisal, the repair list that follows an inspection and the weekend showings. To see what an offer could look like for your address, fill in the form on this page with the house details and the timing you have in mind.

The closing agent reads through the settlement statement with you line by line. It lists the sale price, any mortgage payoff, the tax split, recording costs and what is left for you. Read it before you arrive if the office will send it ahead, and ask about anything that looks different from what you expected.

After the papers are signed, the agent sends the deed to the probate office and pays off any lender. Your proceeds usually arrive by wire or check once the file is recorded. Keep a copy of the signed statement and the tax receipt for your own records, in case a question about the tax year comes up later.

sections.h2: Selling with a mortgage or tax owed
sections.html:
An open mortgage does not stop a sale. The lender sends a payoff figure, the closing agent pays it from the proceeds, and the lien is released when the deed changes hands. If property tax is unpaid, the same thing happens: the balance is cleared at closing so the buyer starts clean.

Where the numbers are tight, ask for the payoff and the tax balance before you list or accept anything, so you know what you would walk away with.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before you pick a closing date
sections.html:
A few answers change how fast a sale can go, and you can get all of them before anyone makes an offer.

  • Is every owner living and able to sign, or is a probate step needed first?
  • Does a lender hold a lien, and what is the payoff today?
  • Is the current tax bill paid, and who is covering the months you will still own the house?
  • Are there tenants, and what does the lease say about notice?
  • Did any storm repair happen, and do you have the receipts?

faqs.q: How many people live in Enterprise, Alabama?
faqs.a: Enterprise had 28,711 residents at the 2020 census. Most of the city is in Coffee County, with part in Dale County.

faqs.q: Is Enterprise close to Fort Rucker?
faqs.a: Yes. The city sits right outside Fort Rucker, the home of Army Aviation.

faqs.q: What tax is due when a deed is recorded in Enterprise?
faqs.a: Alabama's recordation tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, paid before the deed is recorded. The closing agent normally collects it at closing.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Enterprise?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The closing agent usually prorates the year's bill between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Enterprise house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses with old roofs, storm wear or deferred maintenance sell for cash regularly, and you do not need to fix them first.
